module_title: Union Budget 2026-27 - Foundational Matrix (Macro Figures & Tax Baselines)
introduction: The Union Budget 2026-27 is defined by its massive capital expenditure push and strict adherence to fiscal consolidation. Driven by the philosophy of 'Yuva Shakti', it marks the first budget prepared in the newly inaugurated 'Kartavya Bhawan'. At this foundational level, we must memorize the absolute numbers that form the core of the Indian economy.

core_concepts.title: Budget Size and Deficit Targets
core_concepts.description:
- **Total Expenditure:** Estimated at **₹53.47 Lakh Crore** (an increase of 7.7% over the revised estimates of 2025-26).
- **Fiscal Deficit:** Strictly targeted at **4.3% of GDP** for FY 2026-27 (successfully reduced from the 4.4% of the previous fiscal year).
- **Revenue Deficit:** Pegged at **1.5% of GDP**.
- **Nominal GDP Growth:** The government estimates a nominal growth rate (real growth + inflation) of **10%** for FY 2026-27.

core_concepts.title: Capital Expenditure (Capex) Push
core_concepts.description: To sustain infrastructure development as the primary engine of economic growth, Public Capital Expenditure has been significantly enhanced to **₹12.2 Lakh Crore** (up from ₹11.2 Lakh Crore in FY 2025-26). This constitutes a massive commitment to roads, railways, and core asset creation.

core_concepts.title: The '3 Kartavyas' (The Guiding Vision)
core_concepts.description:
The Finance Minister anchored the budget on three foundational duties (Kartavyas):
1. Accelerate and sustain economic growth.
2. Fulfil the aspirations of the people and build their capacity.
3. Align with the vision of 'Sabka Sath, Sabka Vikas' to ensure equitable resource distribution.

core_concepts.title: Taxation Baselines
core_concepts.description: There is **no change** in the income tax slabs for the assessment year 2026-27. However, a landmark structural shift was announced: the highly anticipated **New Income Tax Act, 2025** will officially come into effect from April 2026, introducing drastically simplified rules and compliance forms.

important_entities.name: Fiscal Deficit Consolidation Path
important_entities.significance: In the post-pandemic era, the government has been on a strict glide path to reduce the fiscal deficit. The 4.3% target for FY27 is a critical metric indicating macro-economic stability, making it the most frequently asked data point in banking and civil service prelims.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Examiners will test you on the Tax Collected at Source (TCS) reforms. The TCS on the sale of overseas tour packages and remittances exceeding ₹10 lakh for education or medical purposes has been explicitly reduced from **5% to 2%**. Do not let older data (which had a 20% slab for certain foreign remittances) confuse you.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: A quick recall chain for the biggest macro numbers: Total Expenditure is ₹53+ Lakh Crore, Capex is ₹12.2 Lakh Crore, and Fiscal Deficit is 4.3%.

exam_strategy_tips: For SSC CGL and IBPS exams, direct questions will ask: 'What is the targeted Fiscal Deficit for 2026-27?' or 'What is the total Capital Expenditure?' Lock in the figures **4.3%** and **₹12.2 Lakh Crore**.
